title: One body, one Spirit (Ephesians 4:1–16)
hook: bearing with one another in love, keeping the unity of the Spirit
tomorrow: Paul gives anger a deadline. what time is it due?

segments.voice: Yesterday a prisoner on his knees prayed for more than we ask or think. Today he gets up off the floor and gets practical.
screen: `MORE THAN WE ASK OR THINK.` → `NOW, PRACTICAL.`

segments.voice: Listen for a second to the room you're in: a fridge humming, a car outside, somebody's music through the wall. Lots of sounds, one room. Paul, after three chapters of praise, turns to how people actually live together. And his first instruction isn't a belief. It's a temperament: "With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love." Longsuffering: a long fuse. Forbearing: putting up with each other, on purpose.
screen: `MANY SOUNDS, ONE ROOM.` → `NOT A BELIEF FIRST.` → `A LONG FUSE.`

segments.voice: Then the reason: "Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace." Notice the verb. Keep. Not make, not build from scratch. Paul treats unity as a gift already given, and patience as the guard. Then he lists what holds them together, almost like a chant: "There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all." Here's one to tell a friend: count them. Body, Spirit, hope, Lord, faith, baptism, God. Seven ones, in three verses. One body doesn't mean one kind of person, though. Christ gave "some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers," different roles "for the edifying of the body of Christ." Edifying means building up. Then the body image comes alive, joint by joint: the whole body "fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth." Every joint. Not just the famous ones. Christians today belong to different churches that don't agree on everything, and Paul's word for them all is still keep, guarding the unity with a long fuse, "speaking the truth in love."
screen: `KEEP THE UNITY, DON'T MAKE IT.` · `SEVEN ONES IN THREE VERSES.` · `DIFFERENT GIFTS, ONE BODY.` · `EVERY JOINT SUPPLIETH.` · then, large: `ONE LORD, ONE FAITH.`

segments.voice: Listen to the sounds around you for the sit. Find the one that bothers you, the hum or the neighbor's music, and instead of shutting it out, let it be, on purpose. Then bring to mind one person you find hard to bear, and give them the same patience for a few slow breaths.
One body. Paul's picture of the church as one living body: many joints, many gifts, one Spirit, kept in peace.
Hold onto this: one Lord, one faith, guarded by a long fuse. Go in peace.

fork.setup: a friend on your volunteer team keeps arriving late, and everyone's quietly fuming. what's Paul's way to handle it?
options: speak the truth in love: tell her kindly, to her face.
say nothing ever; forbearing means never bringing it up.
post about it in the group so everyone knows the score.
fork.reveal: Paul pairs patience with honesty: speaking the truth in love. a long fuse isn't silence forever; it's truth said in a way that builds up.

forbearing.meaning: putting up with someone patiently, on purpose
